# Attract to Chat 2.1.3 — Walkie-Chat integration, repaired

Every message you type makes a sound. Somewhere out there, something heard it.

This release re-audits the optional Walkie-Chat integration against the reflection
contracts real Walkie-Chat builds actually ship — and repairs it end to end. Core
gameplay (chat attracts mobs, walls muffle, CAPS shout, Troll Mode, presets, vocal
fatigue, anti-spam) is unchanged and works on both supported Minecraft versions.

## Fixed
- **Hostile mobs now attack Walkie Block stations** — the attraction entry point
  deduces the block target, re-enabling station destruction, the "signal lost"
  notification, and block-target behaviors (creeper ignition, enderman teleport).
- **The station next to you wins** — a hostile already standing near a Walkie Block
  abandons the march to the message and works that station down instead. Nothing is
  deleted in one tick any more: every hostile chips at the block with the game's own
  cracking progress (stages 3 → 6 → 9), a slime hops on top of it, and one mob holds the
  station at a time so a crowd queues and the progress carries over when the worker dies.
  A creeper is the exception — its fuse ends the station outright, and the block goes with
  the blast rather than 1.5 s before it.
- **Plain chat beside a station was swallowed** — typing within reach of a powered Walkie
  Block attracted *nothing*. `suppressesStationChat` trusted Walkie-Chat's
  `findNearbyActiveBlock(ServerPlayer)`, which passes an empty frequency and therefore matches
  any nearby block — walkie in hand or not — so ATC dropped those messages waiting for a relay
  that never re-enters the chat pipeline. Confirmed in the Walkie-Chat 1.3.2 bytecode.
- **A station is a target only when the walkie carried the voice** — the nearby-station detour
  is gone. The sound source becomes the station's own position only when the player holds a
  walkie whose frequency matches a nearby active block; otherwise a message means the player.
- **The wreck costs the network, not a loot roll** — a mob-destroyed station drops nothing.
- **The signal dies over the walkie** — the "signal lost" notice now carries the mod's own
  channel prefix and receive click and names what destroyed the station, to tuned players
  only. The dead `WalkieNetworkHandler` / `isPlayerConnectedToAnyBlock` reflection behind
  the old fallback is gone: neither method exists in Walkie-Chat 1.2.2 or 1.3.2.
- **1.19.2 Forge heard nothing at all** — its chat listener was registered on
  `ServerChatEvent.Submitted`, a class that exists in Forge 43.x but is never posted by the
  1.19.2 chat flow (verified against the runtime jar). Every message was silently ignored on
  that loader. It listens to the real event now.
- **1.19.2 Fabric was deaf whenever Walkie-Chat was installed** — ATC listened to Fabric API's
  chat event, which fires from the vanilla broadcast that Walkie-Chat 1.2.2 cancels in order to
  deliver chat itself, so the event never happened. ATC now hooks the chat packet directly,
  before any mod can intercept it.
- **One documented promise was not implemented** — `/atc walkiechat proximity range|capsbonus`
  had no caller at all; Walkie-Chat now asks ATC for that floor before it reports a range.
- **The toggle truly toggles** — `/atc walkiechat compat enable|disable` now gates
  every part of the integration (chat suppression, station-relayed targets, block
  behavior) symmetrically in both directions.
- **Shared gatekeepers** — the Walkie-Chat reflection path now runs the same
  ignored-players, vocal-fatigue mute and anti-spam checks as normal chat, and
  records per-player stats and debug feedback for relayed messages.
- **Forge canceled-chat handling** — while the integration is on, canceled events still
  reach the engine (Walkie-Chat cancels every event it re-routes); the engine's own
  guards decide what attracts. With the integration off, other mods' cancellations hold.

...

# Attract to Chat 2.1.2 — Forge & Fabric 1.19.2 & 1.20.1

Optional Walkie-Chat integration on Minecraft 1.20.1 — proximity chat, walkie block stations and hostile mob attacks — plus per-player investigation particles on both versions.

- **Fabric 2.1.2** — requires Fabric API 0.92.7+ (1.20.1) or 0.76.0+ (1.19.2).
- **Forge 2.1.2** — no additional dependencies.
- Requires Java 17.
- Server-first: installation on clients is optional.

## New in 2.1.2

- Optional Walkie-Chat compatibility (mod id `walkietalkie`) on Minecraft 1.20.1, enabled by default and toggleable in-game with `/atc walkiechat on|off` or through the `walkieChatCompat` config option. Requires Walkie-Chat 1.3.2 or newer.
- Mobs are attracted to proximity chat spoken through Walkie-Chat, using the effective range Walkie-Chat already resolved; `walkieChatProximityRange` (default 15) and `walkieChatProximityCapsBonus` (default 10) shape the result.
- Hostile mobs that reach an active Walkie Block station destroy it, and every player tuned to its frequency receives a "signal lost" notification in their own language.
- Chat spoken through a handheld walkie or next to an active Walkie Block is routed by Walkie-Chat and is no longer double-processed by the ATC engine.
- `/atc status` reports the Walkie-Chat compatibility state when the mod is present.
- On Minecraft 1.19.2, Walkie-Chat runs side by side without conflicts: walkie talkie chat is never double-processed and normal chat keeps attracting mobs. The walkie talkie integration itself is 1.20.1-only — Walkie-Chat's 1.19.2 builds ship no integration API.

## Changes and fixes

- Removed the server-side `showParticles` master switch: investigation particles are now purely a per-player choice made with `/atc client particles enable|disable`. The `silent` preset no longer touches particles, `/atc status` no longer lists a particle line, and existing configs migrate automatically (schema 17).
- Forge chat handling now listens at the lowest priority and receives canceled events: mods that cancel chat events while re-implementing delivery (Walkie-Chat does) no longer break attraction — ATC's own guards decide what gets processed.
- Fabric chat handling relies on registration order (mods initialize alphabetically by mod id), which places ATC's listener before Walkie-Chat's chat veto.
- Attraction dedupe guard: a message relayed by Walkie-Chat through both its broadcast helper and the block relay attracts mobs only once. The guard keys on message identity and is cleared on server stop, so world reloads never leave it stuck and different messages are never swallowed.

Both Minecraft 1.19.2 and 1.20.1, Forge and Fabric, receive the same code changes; the full Walkie-Chat integration requires Minecraft 1.20.1.

## Downloads

Use the binary JAR matching your loader and Minecraft version. Files ending in `-sources.jar` contain source code for development/reference and are not the playable mod.

# Attract to Chat 2.1.1 — Forge & Fabric 1.19.2 & 1.20.1

Configuration transparency update — every option explained in-game and in the config file itself.

- **Fabric 2.1.1** — requires Fabric API 0.92.7+ (1.20.1) or 0.76.0+ (1.19.2).
- **Forge 2.1.1** — no additional dependencies.
- Requires Java 17.
- Server-first: installation on clients is optional.

## New in 2.1.1

- `/atc config list` shows every option with its current value and default, highlighting anything changed from default.
- `/atc config info <option>` explains any option in plain words: what it does, its unit, default, valid range, and a practical example.
- The config file (`config/attracttochat-common.json`) now carries detailed `#` comments above every option — what it does, unit, default, range, and example — regenerated by the mod on every save.
- `/atc client particles` (no arguments) now reports your current particle preference.
- `/atc help config` documents the new configuration commands.

## Changes and fixes

- Particle preference storage moved from an opt-in UUID list to a per-player on/off map (config schema 15 → 16; existing files migrate automatically on first load).
- Vocal fatigue alert text now describes hoarseness instead of trauma.
- Anti-spam status now reports the cooldown in seconds instead of ticks.
- Removed unused legacy translation keys and dead code paths.
- Config comments are now written without Unicode escapes (`\u0027`-style sequences), keeping the file human-readable in any text editor.

Both Minecraft 1.19.2 and 1.20.1, Forge and Fabric, receive the same changes.

## Downloads

Use the binary JAR matching your loader and Minecraft version. Files ending in `-sources.jar` contain source code for development/reference and are not the playable mod.

# Attract to Chat 2.1.0 for Minecraft 1.19.2

This release brings the complete Attract to Chat 2.1.0 feature set to Minecraft 1.19.2 on Forge and Fabric.

## Highlights

- Chat-driven mob attraction with configurable hearing range and movement.
- Dynamic loudness from CAPS and exclamation marks.
- Terrain Muffling and safe destination resolution.
- Compatible movement for ground, aquatic, flying, and jumping mobs.
- Vanilla combat and villager danger priorities remain respected.
- Ignore rules, Troll Mode, built-in and custom presets.
- Optional Vocal Fatigue and Anti-Spam systems.
- Live configuration, autocomplete, and investigation diagnostics.
- Server-side translations in English, Brazilian Portuguese, and Spanish.
- Optional per-player investigation-path particles.
- Server-side operation without requiring Attract to Chat on connecting clients.
- Forge only reacts to messages after they are submitted; typing and chat previews do not attract mobs.

## Installation

### Fabric 1.19.2

Install Fabric Loader, Fabric API 0.76.0 or newer, and `Attract-To-Chat-1.19.2-Fabric-2.1.0.jar` on the server. Client installation is optional and enables personal path-particle controls.

### Forge 1.19.2

Install Forge 43.4.0 or newer and `Attract-To-Chat-1.19.2-Forge-2.1.0.jar` on the server. Client installation is optional and enables personal path-particle controls.

Java 17 is required. Do not mix Forge and Fabric files.

## Client particles

Players with the optional matching client can use:

```text
/atc client particles enable
/atc client particles disable
```

Particles are disabled by default and are enabled separately by each player.

## Validation status

Both loaders compile and pass automated tests. Dedicated Fabric and Forge development servers reached full startup and stopped cleanly. A real Forge 43.5.0 Prism instance confirmed that typing, editing with Backspace, and canceling chat produce zero attraction scans, while one submitted message produces exactly one scan on the server thread.

The included checklist remains available for broader manual gameplay and mod-compatibility testing.

This is the independent 2.1.0 release line. It contains no Walkie-Chat integration or 2.1.1 feature.

# Attract to Chat 2.1.0 — Fabric 1.20.1 / Forge 2.1.0-r1

Final Minecraft 1.20.1 builds:

- **Fabric 2.1.0** — requires Fabric API 0.92.7 or newer.
- **Forge 2.1.0-r1** — corrected revision that supersedes the previous Forge 2.1.0 build.
- Requires Java 17.
- Server-first: installation on clients is optional.

## Fixes

- Ground mobs now resolve a valid standable destination below airborne chat sources across the configured hearing depth.
- Debug output now reports the heard, attempted, and started movement lifecycle accurately, with readable coordinates.
- Removed the duplicated particle configuration command and improved feedback when particles are already enabled or disabled.
- Fabric now uses the Fabric API message events, ignores command-generated `/say` and `/me` messages, and validates the optional client-presence handshake.
- Declared Fabric API as a required Fabric dependency.
- Added seven regression tests and completed packaged Fabric and Forge manual QA.

## Downloads

Use the binary JAR matching your loader. Files ending in `-sources.jar` contain source code for development/reference and are not the playable mod.
